newsitem.title: TURKEY: More Turkish units said to leave north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: More Turkish units said to leave north Iraq.

text.p: Turkey has completed much of its withdrawal from northern Iraq after a five-week cross-border operation against bases of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), the Anatolian news agency said on Saturday.

"A large portion of the military units has been transferred back into the country. An adequate level of units was left in northern Iraq," military headquarters said in a statement quoted by the state-run agency.
Anatolian said the remaining units were supported by fighters from the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), allied with the Turks against the separatist PKK.
Much of the Arab world and some of Turkey's Western allies have condemned Ankara for its incursion into the Kurdish-held region, cut off by Western air power from Baghdad's control.

The army said 2,601 PKK fighters had been killed and 444 rebels captured in the operation, which began on May 14. At its height the incursion involved more than 10,000 army troops, backed by air power.
It said 99 Turkish soldiers and members of the state-run village guards militia had been killed in Iraq, with 313 injured.
The entire campaign has been carried out under a strict news blackout, with correspondents barred from the region and communications blocked.
Independent confirmation of the army's claims was impossible. However, Ankara-based diplomats say the reported PKK death tolls are exaggerated.
Anatolian said the Turkish army had gained control of the areas of Sinath-Haftanin, Metina, Zap-Amedya, Niverekan-Basyan, Hakurk, Fays Habur, Beyazdag, Dohuk and Gara mountain.
"Under a protocol the cleansed areas will be handed over to (KDP leader Massoud) Barzani," it said.
More than 24,000 people have died in the PKK's 12-year insurgency for self-rule in southeastern Turkey. The latest army statement put total PKK losses for the year at 4,554 fighters.
